[Makkan]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{2} He, exalted is He, informs that this noble Book is a revelation sent down from the Lord of the worlds, who nurtured them with His blessings. Among the greatest of the things with which He nurtured them is this Book, which contains everything that rectifies their conditions and perfects their character. And there is no doubt in it, no uncertainty, and no dispute.

{3} Nevertheless, the deniers of the Messenger, the wrongdoers in this matter, said: "He has invented it; Muhammad has fabricated it from his own self!" This is among the greatest audacity in denying the speech of Allah, and in attributing the greatest falsehood to Muhammad, and [it claims] that creation is capable of producing speech like the speech of the Creator. Each of these is among the grave matters. Allah said, refuting those who said, "He has invented it": {Rather, it is the truth} that falsehood cannot approach from before it or from behind it, a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy. {From your Lord}: He sent it down as a mercy to the servants. {So that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you}; that is, they were in a state of necessity and need for the sending of a Messenger and the revelation of a Book, due to the absence of a warner. Rather, in their ignorance they were wandering blindly, and in the darkness of their misguidance they were hesitating. So We sent the Book down to you {that they may be guided}: from their misguidance, so that they would recognize the truth and prefer it.

All these things that Allah mentioned are contrary to their denial of him, and they require from them faith and complete affirmation of it: that it is from the Lord of the worlds, that it is the truth, and the truth is accepted in every circumstance; that there is no doubt in it in any respect, for there is nothing in it that necessitates doubt, neither in information that does not correspond to reality, nor in obscurity or ambiguity of its meanings; and that they are in necessity and need of the Messenger; and that in it is guidance to every good and benevolence.

{4} He, exalted is He, informs of His perfect power in creating the heavens and the earth in six days, the first of which was Sunday and the last Friday, although He is able to create them in an instant; but He is Gentle and Wise. {Then He istawa (rose) over the Throne}, which is the ceiling of created things, an istiwa' befitting His majesty. {You have not, besides Him, any protector}, who would look after your affairs and benefit you, {nor any intercessor}, who would intercede for you if punishment should be directed at you. {Will you not then remember?} That you would know that the Creator of the earth and the heavens, the One who is established over the Mighty Throne, who alone manages you and takes charge of you, and to whom all intercession belongs, is the One deserving of every kind of worship!

{5} {He arranges every affair}: both the decreed (qadari) matters and the legislated (shar'i) matters; all of them are managed by Him alone, and these arrangements descend from the Sovereign, the All-Powerful, {from the heaven to the earth}. Through them He makes some happy and others wretched, enriches and impoverishes, honors and humiliates, bestows and withholds, raises some peoples and lowers others, and sends down provision. {Then it ascends to Him}; that is, the affair descends from His presence and ascends back to Him {in a Day whose measure is a thousand years of what you count}: it ascends to Him and reaches Him in a moment.

{6} {That}: the One who created those great creatures, who is established over the Mighty Throne, and who alone directs the affairs of the kingdom, {is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful}: by the vastness of His knowledge, the perfection of His might, and the comprehensiveness of His mercy He brought them into being, deposited in them what benefits He deposited, and managing them was not difficult for Him.

{7} {He who perfected everything He created}; that is, every creature God created; indeed God perfected its creation and created it in a manner befitting it and suitable to it. This is general; then He singled out the human being for its nobility and excellence, saying: {And He began the creation of man from clay}: this refers to the creation of Adam, peace be upon him, the father of mankind.

{8} {Then He made his offspring}; that is, the descendants of Adam, produced {from an extract of a worthless fluid}: which is the despised, weak drop (nutfah).

{10} That is: the deniers of resurrection said, expressing it as something far-fetched: {"When we have gone astray in the earth, shall we indeed be in a new creation?"} That is: when we have decayed, been torn apart, and scattered into places that are unknown, shall we indeed be resurrected in a new resurrection? In their claim, this is among the most distant of things! This is because they measure the power of the Creator by their own powers. Their statement is not for seeking the truth; rather, it is injustice, obstinacy, and disbelief in the meeting with their Lord and denial. Therefore He said: {"Nay, they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord."} Thus their statement is known in its source and its end. Otherwise, if their intention were to make the truth clear, the decisive proofs for it would have been made manifest to them, such that it would be witnessed by insight as the sun is witnessed by sight. And it suffices them that they know, by their own knowledge, that they were originated from nothing; so restoration is easier than origination. Likewise, the dead earth, upon which God sends down rain, so it comes to life after its death, and by it the scattered seeds sprout.

{11} {Say: The angel of death who has been entrusted with you will cause you to die.} That is: God has made him an agent (wakil) over the seizing of souls, and he has assistants. {Then to your Lord you will be returned.} He will recompense you for your deeds, and since you denied resurrection, see what God does to you.

{12} When He, the Exalted, mentioned their return to Him on the Day of Resurrection, He mentioned their state as they stand before Him, saying: {And if you could see when the criminals}: those who persisted in the great sins, {will be bowing their heads before their Lord}: humbled and submissive, abased, acknowledging their crime [and] asking for a return, saying: {Our Lord, we have seen and heard}; that is, the matter has become clear to us and we have seen it with our own eyes, so it has become certain knowledge, {so return us, and we will do righteousness. Indeed, we are now certain}; that is, certainty has now arisen in us regarding what we used to deny. And [the meaning is]: you would see a terrible matter, a distressing state, a people who are losers, and a request that will not be granted, because the time of respite has passed.

{13} All of this is by the decree and predestination of Allah, since He left them free between themselves and disbelief and disobedience. Therefore He said: {And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance}; that is, We would have guided all people and gathered them upon guidance. Our will is capable of that, but wisdom refuses that they should all be upon guidance. Therefore He said: {But the word from Me has come into effect: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together"}; that is, it was required and established with an unchanging firmness. {This promise is necessary and there is no escape from it}; therefore the causes of it, namely disbelief and disobedience, must be established.

{14} {So taste [the punishment] for your forgetting the meeting of this your Day}; that is, it will be said to the criminals, whom humiliation has overtaken, and who asked to return to the world in order to make up for what they missed: the time of return has passed, and nothing remains but punishment. So taste the painful punishment for your forgetting the meeting of this your Day. This forgetting is the forgetting of abandonment; that is, for your turning away from it, abandoning work for it, as though you were not going to face it or meet it. {Indeed, We have forgotten you}; that is, We have abandoned you to the punishment as a recompense of the same kind as your deeds; just as you forgot, you are forgotten. {And taste the punishment of eternity}; that is, the punishment that does not cease. For punishment that has a term and an end contains some relief and lightening; but the punishment of Hell, we seek Allah's protection from it, contains no breath of rest and no cessation of their punishment therein. {For what you used to do}: of disbelief, wickedness and disobedience.

Therefore He said: {But the word from Me has come into effect: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together"}; that is, it was required and established with an unchanging firmness. {This promise is necessary and there is no escape from it}; therefore the causes of it, namely disbelief and disobedience, must be established.

{14} {So taste [the punishment] for your forgetting the meeting of this your Day}; that is, it will be said to the criminals, whom humiliation has overtaken, and who asked to return to the world in order to make up for what they missed: the time of return has passed, and nothing remains but punishment. So taste the painful punishment for your forgetting the meeting of this your Day. This forgetting is the forgetting of abandonment; that is, for your turning away from it, abandoning work for it, as though you were not going to face it or meet it. {Indeed, We have forgotten you}; that is, We have abandoned you to the punishment as a recompense of the same kind as your deeds; just as you forgot, you are forgotten. {And taste the punishment of eternity}; that is, the punishment that does not cease. For punishment that has a term and an end contains some relief and lightening; but the punishment of Hell, we seek Allah's protection from it, contains no breath of rest and no cessation of their punishment therein. {For what you used to do}: of disbelief, wickedness and disobedience.

{15} When He mentioned the disbelievers regarding His signs and what He had prepared for them of punishment, He mentioned the believers in them, their description, and what He had prepared for them of reward. He said: ﴿Only those believe in Our signs﴾; that is, true belief is only possessed by those in whom the evidences of faith are found, and they are ﴿those who, when they are reminded﴾ of the signs of their Lord, so that the verses of the Qur'an are recited to them, and admonitions come to them through the hands of the messengers of Allah, and they are called to remembrance; they hear them, accept them, submit, and ﴿fall down in prostration﴾; that is, they humble themselves before them, in the humility of remembrance of Allah and joy at knowing Him, ﴿and glorify the praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant﴾: neither in their hearts nor in their bodies, so that they refuse to submit to them, but rather they are humble before them. They receive them with acceptance and submission, meet them with openness and surrender, and through them they attain the good pleasure of the Most Merciful Lord, and through them they are guided to the Straight Path.

{16} ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾; that is, their sides rise and are drawn away from their pleasant beds toward what is more delightful to them and more beloved to them, which is prayer at night and intimate conversation with Allah, the Exalted. For this reason He said: ﴿They call upon their Lord﴾; that is, to bring about their religious and worldly benefits and to repel their harms, ﴿in fear and in hope﴾; that is, combining the two qualities: fear that their deeds may be rejected, and hope for their acceptance; fear of the punishment of Allah, and hope for His reward. ﴿And from what We have provided them﴾: of provision, little or much, ﴿they spend﴾. He did not mention the restriction of the expenditure, nor the one on whom it is spent, so as to indicate generality. It includes obligatory spending, such as zakat, expiations, and the maintenance of wives and relatives, and recommended spending in the paths of goodness. Spending and financial kindness are good absolutely, whether it benefits a poor or a rich person, a relative or a stranger; but the reward varies according to the variation of benefit. This is their deed.

{17} As for their recompense, He said: ﴿So no soul knows﴾: this includes all the souls of creation, because it is an indefinite noun in the context of negation; that is, no one knows ﴿what has been concealed for them of comfort for their eyes﴾: of abundant good, plentiful bounty, joy, happiness, pleasure and delight; as Allah, the Exalted, said on the tongue of His Messenger: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." Just as they prayed at night, called upon Him, and concealed their deeds, He recompensed them in kind, concealing their reward. For this reason He said: ﴿As a reward for what they used to do.﴾

{18} The Exalted calls the intellects to what is established in them: that two unequal, opposite things are not equal, and that His wisdom requires that they not be equal. So He said: ﴿Is then one who is a believer﴾: whose heart has been made populated by faith, whose limbs have submitted to His laws, and whose faith has required its effects and necessary consequences, namely abandoning the things that anger Allah, whose presence would harm faith; ﴿like one who is defiant?﴾: whose heart has been ruined and rendered idle of faith, so that there is no religious restraint in it, and whose limbs have hastened to the requirements of ignorance and wrongdoing in every sin and disobedience, and who has, through his defiance, departed from obedience to his Lord. Can these two persons be equal?! ﴿They are not equal﴾: by reason and by law; just as night and day, and light and darkness, are not equal. Likewise their reward in the Hereafter is not equal.

{19} ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾: [deeds] of obligatory and voluntary acts; ﴿for them are the Gardens of Refuge﴾; that is, the gardens which are the refuge of pleasures, the source of goods, the place of joys, the bliss of hearts, souls and spirits, the abode of eternity, the neighborhood of the worshipped King, and enjoyment of His nearness, gazing upon His Face and hearing His speech. ﴿As a hospitable welcome﴾ for them; that is, as hospitality and entertainment; ﴿for what they used to do﴾: for their deeds, by which Allah graciously favored them, were what brought them to those lofty, precious abodes, which cannot be reached by spending wealth, nor by soldiers and servants, nor by children, nor even by lives and souls, and nothing at all is approached through except faith and righteous deeds.

{20} ﴿As for those who defied, their refuge is the Fire﴾; that is, their abode and place of eternity is the Fire, which gathers every punishment and misery, and whose punishment is not lightened for them for a moment. ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, they will be returned into it﴾: so whenever their will to exit impels them toward reaching the utmost of punishment, they are returned to it, the spirit of that relief departs from them, and distress intensifies upon them. ﴿And it will be said to them: "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."﴾

This is the punishment of the Fire, in which their abode and refuge lies. As for the punishment that precedes that and serves as its prelude, namely the punishment of the barzakh, it is mentioned by His words:

{21} That is: "And We will surely make the defiant wrongdoers (al-fasiqin al-mukadhdhibin) taste a sample of the lesser punishment (al-adhab al-adna), which is the punishment of the barzakh (the intermediate state between death and resurrection), so that We make them taste a portion of it before they die: either by punishment through killing and the like, as happened to the polytheists of Badr, or at the time of death, as in His saying: ﴿And if you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death, and the angels are stretching out their hands, [saying], "Release your souls. Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation."﴾ Then the lesser punishment will be completed for them in their barzakh."

This verse is among the evidences for the affirmation of the punishment of the grave, and its indication is clear. For He said: ﴿And We will surely make them taste the lesser punishment﴾, meaning some part and portion of it. This shows that there is a lesser punishment before the greater punishment, which is the punishment of the Fire. Since tasting the lesser punishment in this world may not be followed by death, He, exalted is He, informed that He will make them taste that, so that perhaps they will return to Him and repent of their sins, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea by what the hands of people have earned, that He may let them taste part of that which they have done, so that they may return.﴾

{22} That is: there is no one more wrongful and more transgressive than the one who is reminded of the signs of his Lord, which his Lord conveyed to him, the Lord who wishes to nurture him and perfect His favour upon him through His messengers. They command him and remind him of his religious and worldly interests, and forbid him from what harms him in religion and in worldly life. These demand that he respond to them with faith, submission, compliance and gratitude. Yet this wrongdoer responded to them with the opposite of what was fitting: he did not believe in them nor follow them, but turned away from them and cast them behind his back. This is among the greatest of the criminals, who deserve severe retribution. For this reason He said: {Indeed, We will take retribution upon the criminals.}

{23} When Allah, may He be exalted, mentioned His verses by which He reminds His servants, namely the Qur'an which He sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ), He mentioned that it is not an innovation among the books, nor is the one who brought it a strange messenger among the messengers. Allah gave {Musa the Book}, which is the Torah, confirming the Qur'an, and the Qur'an confirmed it, so their truth coincides and their proof is established. {So be not in doubt about meeting Him}, because the proofs of the truth and its clear evidences have come in succession, so no place remains for doubt and suspicion. {And We made it}, i.e., the Book that We gave Musa, {a guidance for the Children of Israel}, by which they would be guided in the foundations of their religion and its branches. Its legislation suited that time among the Children of Israel. As for this noble Qur'an, Allah made it a guidance for all people, because it is a guidance for creation in the matters of their religion and their worldly affairs until the Day of Resurrection, and that is due to its perfection and sublimity. {And indeed it is, in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and full of wisdom}.

{24} {And We made from among them}, i.e., from among the Children of Israel, {leaders guiding by Our command}, i.e., scholars of the Sharia and the paths of guidance, who are themselves guided and guide others with that guidance. The Book that was sent down to them is a guidance, and those among them who believed in it are of two categories: leaders who guide by Allah's command, and followers who are guided by them. The first category has the highest rank after the rank of prophethood and messengerhood, which is the rank of the truthful (siddiqin). They attained this high rank {because they were patient}, in learning, teaching, calling to Allah, and enduring harm in His path, and they restrained their souls from their unbridled disobedience and their indulgence in desires. {And they were certain of Our signs}, i.e., they reached, in faith in Allah's signs, the level of certainty (yaqin), which is complete knowledge that necessitates action. They reached the level of certainty because they learned properly and took matters from their evidences that produce certainty. They continued to learn the issues and to derive proofs for them through abundant evidences until they reached that. Thus, by patience and certainty, leadership in religion is attained.

{25} There are matters about which the Children of Israel differed: some of them were correct in them, and some of them missed the truth, either by error or deliberately. Allah, may He be exalted, {will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ}. This Qur'an relates to the Children of Israel some of what they differ about. So every disagreement that arose among them, and in which the Qur'an is found to confirm one of the two views, that is the truth, and whatever opposes it is falsehood.

{26} That is, "Have they not been shown clearly—these deniers of the Messenger—and has it not guided them to the right way, how many generations We destroyed before them, who followed their same path, {walking in their dwellings}: so they witness them with their own eyes, like the people of Hud, Salih and the people of Lut." {Indeed in that are signs}: by which one may infer the truthfulness of the messengers who came to them, and the falsehood of what they were upon of shirk and evil, and that whoever does the like of their deeds will be dealt with as those who were like them were dealt with before, and that Allah, exalted is He, recompenses the servants and resurrects them for the gathering and the calling-out. {Will they not then listen}: to the signs of Allah, so that they comprehend them and benefit from them? For if they had sound hearing and sound reasoning, they would not persist in a state for which destruction is certain.

{27} {Have they not seen}: with their eyes, Our blessing and the perfection of Our wisdom, {that We drive the water to the barren land}: in which there is no vegetation, so Allah drives the rain, which previously did not exist there, and pours it onto it from the clouds or from the rivers; {and We bring forth thereby crops}; that is, plants of varied kinds, {of which their cattle eat}: and that is the fodder of the beasts, {and they themselves}: and that is the food of the children of Adam. {Will they not then see}: that favour by which Allah gives life to the lands and the servants, so that they may perceive and be guided by that sight and that insight to the straight path? But blindness has overcome them, and heedlessness has taken hold of them, so they did not look at that with the sight of men, but only looked at it with the glance of heedlessness and mere habit, and so they were not granted success in goodness.

**28.** That is: the criminals hasten the punishment that they were promised for denying the message, out of ignorance and obstinacy. ﴿And they say, "When is this victory?"﴾ That is, the decisive judgment that will settle matters between us and you, by punishing us, as you claim, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ [O messengers] in your claim.

**29.** ﴿Say: "On the Day of Victory"﴾ (the day on which your punishment takes place), ﴿your faith will not benefit you at all.﴾ For if, when it occurred, a respite were granted so that you could make up what you missed once the matter had become certain to you, there would be some sense to that. But when the Day of Victory comes, the matter is over, and no place remains for trial and testing. So ﴿their faith will not benefit those who disbelieved,﴾ because it has become a faith of compulsion, ﴿nor will they be granted respite﴾; that is, they will not be given time, so that the punishment would be delayed and they could then set their affairs right.

**30.** ﴿So turn away from them﴾, since their address to you and their wrongdoing have reached the point of ignorance and of hastening the punishment. ﴿And wait﴾ for the matter that will befall them, for it is inevitable, but it has a fixed term, and when it comes it will neither advance nor be delayed. ﴿Indeed, they are waiting﴾ for you to suffer the calamities of fate (rayb al-manun), and they are lying in wait for you with the cycles of evil, while the final outcome belongs to righteousness (taqwa).

The tafsir of Surah as-Sajdah is complete, by the power and favour of God. To Him, the Exalted, belongs perfect praise, commendation and glory.
